StackType.issue: The sim drops a re-application's offset on the strength of a misreading of PowerStackType.Single. Single means only 'Amount is hidden, and is always 1' (PowerStackType.cs:10-13); PowerCmd.ModifyAmount:236 adds the offset with no StackType branch, so playing Hellraiser twice gives C# Amount 2 and the sim Amount 1. DORMANT for this unit -- Hellraiser reads Amount nowhere, so the value is inert. Recorded because this is one of 15 ported powers that make the same misreading (reproduce with `py audit/tools/power_census.py stack`), and for the others Amount is load-bearing. Named trigger: any Hellraiser behaviour that reads Amount. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterCardDrawnEarly.issue: NARROWED 2026-07-28. Clause (a), PHASE LOSS, is CLOSED. The sim now has real phase passes and this listener is on the Early one: HellraiserPower.on_card_drawn_early (sts2_rl/powers.py:762) is picked up by HookSystem._each's `_very_early -> _early -> plain -> _late` walk (sts2_rl/hooks.py:36 _PHASES, :153-180 _each), which HookSystem.on_card_drawn (sts2_rl/hooks.py:591-599) dispatches through, and `_phase_hooks(HellraiserPower)` returns {'on_card_drawn'} (executed from the repo root), so the auto-play completes before any plain on_card_drawn listener sees the draw -- exactly as Hook.AfterCardDrawn runs AfterCardDrawnEarly over every listener (Hook.cs:204-211) before AfterCardDrawn (Hook.cs:212-218). WHAT REMAINS is clause (b), unchanged: the 9-auto-play safety cap is still absent, and the sim's own docstring still justifies the omission with a claim that is FALSE. sts2_rl/powers.py:762-770 is the entire port -- Strike-tag test, combat.is_over test, combat.auto_play_card -- with no per-turn counter, no `_infiniteAutoPlayCap` and no reset, where HellraiserPower.cs:26 declares the cap, :45-57 increments `infiniteAutoPlaysThisTurn` and refuses the auto-play at 9 whenever `Owner.CombatState.HittableEnemies.All(c => c.HpDisplay.IsInfinite())`, and :70-78 / :91-96 clear it at AfterSideTurnEnd. powers.py:752-753 still says the cap applies 'only against infinite-HP enemies, which the sim does not have', but both C# HpDisplay.IsInfinite sites are ported: SteamEruptionPower drives hp = max_hp = 999_999_999 (sts2_rl/powers.py:2151, class at :2115) and HardenedShellPower is ported at sts2_rl/powers.py:2066. A second, smaller remainder at the same site: HellraiserPower.cs:39's `card.Owner.Creature != base.Owner` ownership gate has no counterpart -- powers.py:765 tests only the Strike tag (dormant while the sim has one player and Hellraiser is player-only). STILL DORMANT overall, for the reason the original gave and the docstring does not: an auto-played Strike goes to the discard pile rather than back to the draw pile, so nothing ported can draw 10 Strikes in one turn. Named trigger unchanged: any effect that returns Strikes to the draw pile mid-turn while the only hittable enemy shows infinite HP.  NARROWED 2026-07-28 (Task 0, ledger-vs-code pass after the Tier 1 fix campaign): the rest of this entry is closed in today's code. The issue it replaced read: Two divergences. (a) PHASE LOSS. This is a phase-suffixed C# hook and the sim has a single unphased dispatch, which is hook_dispatch gap G3 (24 dispatchers lose their phase structure; 27 phase-suffixed hooks declared on AbstractModel). Per binding rule 3 the mechanism keeps G3's `gap` verdict and is cross-referenced rather than re-argued. Third-file citations, not hashed here. AfterCardDrawnEarly is one of the nine phase-suffixed hooks hook_dispatch step 28 enumerates; the sim's on_card_drawn is the only pass there is, so Hellraiser's auto-play races every other on_card_drawn listener by registration order instead of running strictly first. That matters here more than usual, because auto-playing the drawn card CHANGES what later listeners see. (b) The 9-auto-play safety cap (HellraiserPower.cs:26,45-57,91-96) is absent, and the sim's own docstring justifies the omission with a claim that is FALSE: it says the cap applies 'only against infinite-HP enemies, which the sim does not have' (powers.py:696-698), but C#'s HpDisplay.IsInfinite (HpDisplayExtensions.cs:8-15) is set at exactly two sites and the sim ports BOTH -- WaterfallGiant.cs:306 (SteamEruptionPower drives the sim to hp = max_hp = 999_999_999, powers.py:2033) and HardenedShellPower.cs:66 (ported at powers.py:1955-2001). Per binding rule 5 an unreachability claim has to be executed, and this one does not survive being checked. DORMANT anyway, for a reason the docstring does not give: the cap is a runaway guard, and an auto-played Strike goes to the discard pile rather than back to the draw pile, so nothing ported can draw 10 Strikes in one turn. Named trigger: any effect that returns Strikes to the draw pile mid-turn while the only hittable enemy shows infinite HP. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: HellraiserPower.cs:70-78 resets the per-turn infinite-auto-play counter. The sim tracks no counter (see the AfterCardDrawnEarly entry), so there is nothing to reset. Dormant for the same reason and with the same trigger; carried separately because a fix for the cap must add this reset too, and because the harness requires a verdict per override.

BeforeAttack.rationale: HellraiserPower.cs:80-89 only decorates the AttackCommand with hit VFX, a cast animation and hit-VFX placement. Presentation.

guards.rationale: `card.Owner.Creature != base.Owner` reduces to a tautology in the sim: there is one player, every Card belongs to it, and this power is only ever applied to the player. Same reading power_cmd's sim-entry note and SurroundedPower's own comment (powers.py:2574-2576) already record.
powers.py:708 `'strike' not in card.tags`. Identical -- keyed on the Strike TAG, not on the card id or type, so Perfected Strike-style tagged cards behave the same on both sides.

powers.py:711-712 refuses to auto-play once the combat is over. C# needs no such test because Hook.IterateCombatHookListeners yields nothing to a dispatch begun after combat starts ending (Hook.cs:53-63) -- the sim's missing gate is hook_dispatch gap G8, and this power hand-rolls the specific case. Not a divergence: it makes the sim MORE like the game here. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

HellraiserPower.cs:65 passes target null; combat.auto_play_card (combat.py:517-...) picks a random living enemy off Rng.CombatTargets for an ANY_ENEMY card, which is CardCmd.cs:77's behaviour. The autoPlayingCards set (:19,64,66) exists only to drive the BeforeAttack VFX, so its absence is part of that waiver.
